w:r.w:t: Use D3 to generate a simple bar chart from a csv file to replace a static chart on your Energy Consumption website.

So far you have processed some data and generated some charts using KNIME and/or Excel and displayed them as images in a webpage. However, your ability to customise the chart and allow the user to interact was very limited. In this exercise we will use D3 to build a bar chart of some data from the TV energy consumption data set.

While it is possible to get GenAI to write you code for creating a bar chart with our data set, it is suggested that you work through these exercises so you can see how the data and svgs are attached to the DOM using D3.

Learn how to load and format data so it is ready for D3.

Previously we have processed our data in KNIME. We have used nodes such as GroupBy to obtain summary tables of our data for attributes such as Screen Technology or Brand which we have plotted in KNIME.
In this activity we will look at loading data from a CSV file into D3 so it is ready to chart.
Make sure you have a 'data' folder in your project.
Use the KNIME CSV Writer node to write one of your data summary tables to a csv file and add the new csv to your data folder.
The csv should have at least one category attribute (e.g., brand, screen technology, screensize (as a string)) and one numerical attribute (e.g., count, Star2, Labelled energy consumption etc).

Create a variety of different chart types using D3.

So far we have learnt a lot just by making a simple horizontal bar chart. In this activity we take it a few steps further to make a variety of common chart types. A set of csv files have been prepared that will allow you to make the following charts:
Scatter plot (energy consumption vs star rating)
Donut-chart (energy consumption for different screen technologies across all TVs combined)
Bar chart (energy consumption for different screen technologies for 55inch TVs only)
Line chart (spot power prices from 1998 to 2024) (you can plot average only, or have a line for each state)
You can use your own data sets and questions, or the
but you must have an example of each chart type.
It is recommended that you review this week's lecture and review

Your charts should all appear on the one web page. Each chart should have its own js file.
They should change size depending on the size of the user's window.
They should be well placed on the screen and ideally include some introductory text.
The following is an example of the type of thing you should be aiming for:
You should try to customise your page to follow good data visualisation guidelines where possible (do not try to replicate this screenshot exactly, it does not follow good design principles).

When using GenAI take care in phrasing your questions. Don't forget to ask it for different more efficient or best practice ways of doing things and ask it to explain the code it provides.
Build a histogram and add interactive filters.

Interaction is one of the key advantages of displaying visualisations on a computer. In this exercise you will build a histogram based on the TV data set and add interactive filters such that users can explore the energy consumption of LCD, LED and OLED TVs in the data set.
